title: FaultInsight: Interpreting Hyperscale Data Center Host Faults

problem.claim: Diagnosing root causes of failures across millions of hyperscale data-center service hosts requires substantial operator effort.

gap.claim: Existing time-series causal-discovery methods focus on homogeneous service-level performance metrics and do not provide useful insights for heterogeneous host-level metrics.

contributions.claim: FaultInsight is an interpretable deep causal framework for diagnosing host faults from multiple perspectives.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors evaluated FaultInsight on dozens of incidents collected from their production environment.
The authors report markedly better root-cause identification accuracy than SOTA baselines on their incident dataset.
The authors report advantages in deployability and say their engineers found its multi-perspective incident interpretations helpful for understanding fault mechanisms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyperscale data-center operation involves diagnosing frequent failures across millions of hosts.
Existing causal-discovery approaches are limited to homogeneous service-level metrics and fail to explain heterogeneous host-level metrics usefully.
FaultInsight is introduced as an interpretable deep causal host-fault diagnosis framework providing multiple diagnostic perspectives.
The framework is evaluated on dozens of production incidents, with reported accuracy and deployability advantages over SOTA baselines.

source_observation.claim: Existing methods focus on homogeneous service-level metrics, while the proposed framework addresses heterogeneous host-level metrics.

interpretation.claim: Diagnostic systems may need to model heterogeneity explicitly rather than applying service-level assumptions to host-level faults.

application.claim: When designing operational diagnosis tools, integrate heterogeneous host-level signals and expose interpretable views for troubleshooting.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported production incidents or data-center setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the causal model, input metrics, or diagnostic perspectives.
The abstract does not provide incident counts, accuracy values, baseline details, or statistical methodology.
The abstract does not describe deployment scale, computational requirements, or failure cases.
